results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response:
The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. VFB records show that the mushroom body is divided into these three parts, with the calyx receiving sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus being a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes, and the mushroom body lobe system consisting of a vertical branch and a medial branch. 

VFB holds a range of data related to the mushroom body, including images, neuron information, parts, subclasses, and lineage clones. For example, VFB has annotated [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, and [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of the mushroom body. The user can explore these data further by querying the VFB database.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as recorded in VFB. According to VFB, the giant fiber neuron has a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum and a large descending axon that is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective. This information is based on publications by Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Namiki et al. (2018), and Power (1948). 

VFB holds [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of the DNp01 neuron, which is associated with the giant fiber neuron. There are also [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting DNp01 and [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01. The downstream connectivity classes for DNp01 are represented by [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records in VFB, while the upstream connectivity classes are represented by [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records. 

The giant fiber neuron's connectivity can be described as having dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, and its axon enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side in the dorsal cervical fasciculus. 

Relevant publications for the giant fiber neuron include those by Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Namiki et al. (2018), Power (1948), and Ito et al. (2014), as cited in VFB.
